series.title: Stance & balance
series.summary: How ski stance, outside-ski pressure, and ankle flexion create control.

articles.title: Trust the outside ski
articles.body:
In a turn, most of your pressure belongs on the outside ski. That ski draws the arc; the inside ski guides and balances.

Beginners often stand equally on both skis and skid. Intermediate skiers start tipping earlier so the outside edge can grip before the fall line.

A simple cue: feel the shin against the tongue of the outside boot through the middle of the turn.

articles.title: Ankle flexion first
articles.body:
Good ski balance starts in the ankles, not the hips. Flexing the ankles moves you over the skis so edges engage underfoot.

If you fold only at the waist, tips lighten and the tails wash. Keep the torso quiet and tip from the boots up.

series.title: Reading ski snow
series.summary: Hardpack, soft snow, and flat light — how conditions change turn shape.

articles.title: Hardpack rewards early edges
articles.body:
On firm snow, late pressure becomes a skid. Tip earlier, shorten the radius, and keep hands quiet.

Ice patches in shade lines need intentional edge angle — hope is not a strategy.

articles.title: Flat light tactics
articles.body:
When contrast disappears, slow down and use shorter turns. Follow trees, markers, and other tracks you can still see.

Trust the fall line more than faded visual detail.
